scope_note: The registry contains every AS or AS/NZS document directly referenced in the national ABCB Housing Provisions column of NCC Schedule 2, updated by NCC 2022 Amendment 2, plus supporting standards needed by researched physical-object families. classification_note: Ontology relevance and discipline tags are Basegrid research-triage classifications, not classifications assigned by the NCC or Standards Australia.

standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2022 edition for certified mechanical backflow prevention devices.

standards.title: Testing of products for use in contact with drinking water

notes: Conformance is product evidence, not a drawable material.

standards.title: Safety and public health requirements for plumbing products — Water heaters and hot-water storage tanks
standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2020 edition for instantaneous, storage, solar and heat-exchange water heaters and storage.

standards.title: Valves primarily for use in heated water systems, Part 1: Protection valves
standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2019 edition for expansion-control and temperature/pressure-relief valves.

standards.title: Valves primarily for use in heated water systems, Part 2: Control valves

standards.title: Water supply — Valves for the control of heated water supply temperatures, Part 1: Thermostatic mixing valves

standards.title: Water supply — Valves for the control of heated water supply temperatures, Part 2: Tempering valves and end-of-line temperature-actuated devices

standards.title: Water supply — Valves for the control of heated water supply temperatures, Part 3: Requirements for field-testing, maintenance or replacement of valves, taps and devices
standards.current_publication_note: The 2022 edition superseded AS 4032.3-2004.
notes: Testing and maintenance records are evidence, not physical objects.

standards.title: PVC-U pipes and fittings for drain, waste and vent applications

standards.title: PVC-U pipes and fittings for stormwater and surface water applications
standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2010 edition for PVC-U stormwater and surface-water pipework.

standards.title: PVC pipes and fittings for pressure applications
standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2017 edition for PVC pressure pipes and fittings.

standards.title: Polyethylene pipes for pressure applications
standards.current_publication_note: WaterMark lists the 2018 edition for PE pressure pipes.

standards.title: Solar and heat pump water heaters — Design and construction
standards.current_publication_note: Reconfirmed in Australia in 2019 and New Zealand in 2020.

standards.title: Water efficient products — Rating and labelling
standards.current_publication_note: NCC Volume Three explanatory material identifies this as the basis of WELS product rating and labelling.
notes: A WELS rating is product evidence, not an extra physical component.

standards.title: Water supply — Flexible hose assemblies
standards.current_publication_note: The 2025 AS/NZS 3500.1 and 3500.4 revisions added provisions aligned with this product standard.

standards.title: Heated water systems — Calculation of energy consumption
standards.current_publication_note: NCC Volume Three references the 2021 edition for heated-water energy calculation.
notes: Energy results remain metadata attached to the selected system.

standards.title: Gas fired water heaters for hot water supply and/or central heating
standards.current_publication_note: NCC Volume Three Schedule 2 names the 2005 edition for the water-heater product family.
notes: Gas supply and flue installation are separate regulatory domains.

standards.title: Electrical installations (known as the Australian/New Zealand Wiring Rules)
standards.current_publication_note: Published with amendments 1:2020, 2:2021 and 3:2023 and Ruling 1:2024 shown as current public metadata. The legally applicable consolidation and jurisdictional adoption must be checked for each project.
notes: This is the principal supporting electrical-installation path for the house-scale physical objects; it is not a direct national Housing Provisions Schedule 2 call-up.

standards.title: Electrical installations — Selection of cables, Part 1.1: Cables for voltages up to and including 0.6/1 kV a.c. and up to and including 1500 V d.c. — Typical Australian installation conditions
standards.current_publication_note: Published 19 December 2025. Public WA guidance required full use from 19 June 2026 after its transition; other jurisdictional adoption must be checked separately.
notes: Cable size, current-carrying capacity, voltage drop and derating remain calculated instance metadata, not distinct physical-object classes.

standards.title: Electrical installations — Construction and demolition sites
standards.current_publication_note: Public Standards Australia guidance identifies the 2019 edition for construction and demolition site installations.
notes: Only materially relevant temporary physical equipment is modelled; testing regimes and site procedures remain evidence metadata.

standards.title: Electrical installations — Verification by inspection and testing
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata records the 2022 edition as current.
notes: Inspection results, certificates and test values are evidence attached to installed objects, not geometry.

standards.title: Approval and test specification — Plugs and socket-outlets
standards.current_publication_note: Published in 2025 with a product transition described by Queensland's Electrical Safety Office; the preceding 2017 edition and amendment may remain relevant during transition or to existing products.
notes: Covers product configurations and safety evidence; it does not by itself determine outlet location, circuit design or installation compliance.

standards.title: Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear assemblies, Part 3: Distribution boards intended to be operated by ordinary persons (DBO)
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata records the 2016 Part 3 publication for household and similar distribution-board products.
notes: The complete installed switchboard also depends on its enclosure, devices, connections, labels and project installation path.

standards.title: Residual current operated circuit-breakers with integral overcurrent protection for household and similar uses (RCBOs), Part 1: General rules
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata shows Amendment 1:2024 to the 2015 publication.
notes: An RCBO combines residual-current and overcurrent functions in one device; RCD is a broader function and must not be treated as a shape synonym.

standards.title: Installation and safety requirements for photovoltaic (PV) arrays
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public material records the 2021 revision and its alternative array-isolation arrangements.
notes: Do not draw a rooftop DC isolator by default; isolation equipment is selected from the documented system arrangement.

standards.title: Grid connection of energy systems via inverters, Part 1: Installation requirements
standards.current_publication_note: The 2024 edition replaced the 2016 installation publication; distributor connection rules and transition dates remain project inputs.
notes: Network approval, export limits and inverter settings are metadata, not extra objects.

standards.title: Electrical installations — Safety of battery systems for use with power conversion equipment
standards.current_publication_note: Amendment 1:2025 was published on 19 December 2025. NSW and WA public guidance records jurisdiction-specific commencement or transition information.
notes: Battery location, barriers and clearance zones must come from the selected product, installation category, licensed standard and jurisdiction; they are not universal solids.

standards.title: Installation requirements for customer cabling (Wiring Rules)
standards.document_kind: Australian Standard / Communications Alliance industry code
standards.current_publication_note: ACMA identifies the 2020 edition under the Telecommunications Cabling Provider Rules 2025.
notes: Registration, competency and cabling records remain evidence; cables, pathways, distributors and outlets are physical objects.

standards.title: Requirements for customer cabling products
standards.document_kind: Australian Standard / Communications Alliance industry code
standards.current_publication_note: ACMA identifies the 2020 edition for customer-cabling products under current regulatory instruments.
notes: Product compliance is evidence attached to cable and connecting hardware, not a separate drawable object.

standards.title: Luminaires, Part 2.2: Particular requirements — Recessed luminaires and recessed air-handling luminaires
standards.current_publication_note: Published 26 June 2026. Standards Australia public history identifies AS/NZS 60598.2.2:2016 as the previous edition; product transition and regulator adoption must be checked.
notes: Insulation-contact classification and installation clearances are selected-product evidence; do not infer them solely from the object name downlight.

standards.title: The use of ventilation and airconditioning in buildings, Part 2: Mechanical ventilation in buildings
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia describes the 2024 edition as replacing AS 1668.2:2012. The Housing Provisions schedule used here still directly calls up the 2012 edition.
notes: Use as supporting current technical context only unless the applicable regulatory instrument adopts it.

standards.title: Residential heating and cooling systems — Minimum applications and requirements for energy efficiency, performance and comfort criteria
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia published the 2018 edition for residential climate-control design, selection, installation, commissioning and maintenance.
notes: Supporting residential HVAC standard; not directly called up by the Housing Provisions schedule used here.

standards.title: Refrigerating systems and heat pumps — Safety and environmental requirements, Part 1: Definitions, classification and selection criteria
standards.current_publication_note: The 2016 Australian/New Zealand adoption is recorded as supporting refrigerating-system terminology and selection context.
notes: Not directly called up by the Housing Provisions schedule used here.

standards.title: Refrigerating systems and heat pumps — Safety and environmental requirements, Part 2: Design, construction, testing, marking and documentation
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public metadata lists the 2016 edition for refrigerating-system design, construction and installation-associated components.
notes: Not directly called up by the Housing Provisions schedule used here.

standards.title: Refrigerating systems and heat pumps — Safety and environmental requirements, Part 3: Installation site
standards.current_publication_note: The 2016 Australian/New Zealand adoption is recorded for supporting installation-site and equipment-location context.
notes: Clearance, refrigerant-charge and room-volume results are project analysis, not physical objects inferred from generic geometry.

standards.title: Refrigerating systems and heat pumps — Safety and environmental requirements, Part 4: Operation, maintenance, repair and recovery
standards.current_publication_note: The 2016 Australian/New Zealand adoption is recorded for supporting service access, recovery and maintenance context.
notes: Licences, service records and recovery procedures are evidence or activities, not drawable system members.

standards.title: Refrigerants — Designation and safety classification
standards.current_publication_note: The 2016 Australian/New Zealand adoption is recorded for refrigerant identity and safety-class metadata.
notes: Refrigerant is stored as system and product metadata; the contained fluid is not a separate building solid in ordinary SketchUp output.

standards.title: Household and similar electrical appliances — Safety, Part 2.40: Particular requirements for electrical heat pumps, air-conditioners and dehumidifiers
standards.current_publication_note: Published 27 November 2025 as the current appliance-safety edition in Standards Australia public metadata; product transition and regulatory adoption remain project checks.
notes: Product compliance is evidence attached to selected equipment, not something proven by a generic model shape.

standards.title: Performance of electrical appliances — Air conditioners and heat pumps, Part 1.1: Non-ducted air conditioners and heat pumps — Testing and rating for performance
standards.current_publication_note: The Australian Government GEMS air-conditioner determination identifies this edition for specified regulated performance paths.
notes: Ratings are product evidence, not additional physical objects.

standards.title: Performance of electrical appliances — Air conditioners and heat pumps, Part 1.2: Ducted air conditioners and air-to-air heat pumps — Testing and rating for performance
standards.current_publication_note: The Australian Government GEMS air-conditioner determination identifies this edition for specified regulated performance paths.
notes: Ratings are product evidence, not additional physical objects.

standards.title: Gypsum linings — Application and finishing
standards.current_publication_note: Use the 2017 base publication together with Amendment 1:2018 and Amendment 2:2021 where this supporting standard applies. The selected NCC Housing Provisions baseline does not directly call it up.
notes: Supports identification of substrates, sheets, fasteners, adhesives, tapes, beads, control joints and finishing materials; licensed clauses and dimensions are not reproduced.

standards.title: Suspended ceilings — Design and installation
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2020 edition. It is supporting ceiling-system evidence rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Loads, bracing, seismic restraint, suspension spacing and structural fixings require project and selected-system design; they cannot be inferred from generic grid geometry.

standards.title: Adhesives — For bonding gypsum plaster linings to wood and metal framing members
standards.current_publication_note: The 2018 publication with Amendment 1:2021 is recorded as supporting product evidence and is not a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Adhesive compatibility, bead or daub pattern and curing requirements remain selected-product and substrate data.

standards.title: Plywood and blockboard for interior use
standards.current_publication_note: Public government metadata records the 2006 edition, Amendment 1 incorporated and reconfirmation in 2016 for fully protected interior plywood and blockboard.
notes: This product scope does not make an interior plywood sheet structural, wet-area suitable or fire-compliant; those are separate selected-product and project checks.

standards.title: Timber and composite doors
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2017 edition as current. It is supporting product and installation evidence rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Supports timber and composite flush-panel and joinery door or doorset families; fire, acoustic, thermal and other specialised performance require separate evidence.

standards.title: Locksets and hardware for doors and windows — Glossary of terms and rating system
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2008 edition and Amendment 1 as current. It is a supporting terminology and rating standard, not a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: A hardware rating is selected-product evidence and is not inferred from a generic handle, latch or lock shape.

standards.title: Locksets and hardware for doors and windows — Mechanical locksets for doors and windows in buildings
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2008 edition as current with reconfirmation history. It is supporting lockset evidence rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Function, security, durability and corrosion results belong to a selected tested product; the ontology separately models its physical parts.

standards.title: Locksets and hardware for doors and windows — Controlled door closing devices
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2011 edition with Amendment 1:2013 as current. It is supporting closer evidence rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: A generic closer does not establish suitability for a fire door, accessible path, leaf mass or opening-force requirement; those checks stay attached to the selected doorset and project path.

standards.title: Particleboard flooring — Installation
standards.current_publication_note: The 2006 edition incorporating Amendment 1:2010 is current and is directly called up by NCC Volume Two H1D6. It is not counted as a direct ABCB Housing Provisions Schedule 2 reference.
notes: Supports selection, placement and fixing anatomy for Class 1 particleboard structural flooring; spans and fixing details require the licensed edition and selected product.

standards.title: Particleboard flooring — Specifications
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata records the 2017 edition as current. The product is intended to be installed in accordance with AS 1860.2.
notes: Product classification and compliance belong to the selected sheet; the ontology models the physical sheet and installation components separately.

standards.title: Floor coverings — Resilient sheet and tiles — Installation practices
standards.current_publication_note: The current 2021 edition supersedes AS 1884-2012. It is supporting floor-covering practice rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Covers resilient PVC, hybrid modular, linoleum, rubber and self-adhesive tile installation; carpet, timber and cork products are outside its public scope.

standards.title: Textile floor coverings — Installation practice, Part 1: General
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public catalogue metadata lists the 2019 edition as current. It is supporting carpet-installation evidence, not a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Supports general subfloor, underlay, broadloom, fixing, seam and transition roles without supplying universal dimensions.

standards.title: Textile floor coverings — Installation practice, Part 2: Carpet tiles
standards.current_publication_note: Public standards metadata lists the 2019 edition as current. It is supporting carpet-tile installation evidence rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Carpet tile remains a modular textile finish, not a cut piece of broadloom carpet.

standards.title: Soft underlays for textile floor coverings
standards.current_publication_note: The 2003 edition was reconfirmed in 2016 and remains current according to public standards metadata.
notes: Supports fibrous, non-fibrous and combination carpet-underlay families; use classification remains selected-product evidence.

standards.title: Timber flooring — Sanding and finishing
standards.current_publication_note: The 2005 edition was reconfirmed in 2016 and remains current in public metadata. No general AS 4786 Part 1 installation publication was identified.
notes: Supports sanding, filling, sealing and coating anatomy for strip and parquetry floors; installation is sourced separately.

standards.title: Timber — Hardwood — Sawn and milled products, Part 1: Product specification
standards.current_publication_note: The 1999 edition was reconfirmed in 2016 and remains current according to public metadata.
notes: Supports solid hardwood strip-flooring and parquetry product identity; grade and moisture content remain selected-product attributes.

standards.title: Timber — Softwood — Sawn and milled products, Part 1: Product specification
standards.current_publication_note: The 2002 edition was reconfirmed in 2016 and remains current according to public metadata.
notes: Supports tongue-and-groove softwood strip-flooring product identity; grade and moisture content remain selected-product attributes.

standards.title: Ceramic tiles — Definitions, classification, characteristics and marking
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public metadata lists the 2020 edition as current. It supports tile product identity rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Accessory pieces, trims and mosaics are not collapsed into the generic tile unit; installation remains linked to AS 3958:2023.

standards.title: Guide to the painting of buildings
standards.current_publication_note: The current 2017 edition incorporates Amendment 1:2019. Public scope covers decorative building-paint systems and excludes the long-term atmospheric protection of iron and steel addressed by the AS/NZS 2312 series.
notes: A guide to building painting does not itself select a proprietary product, coating thickness or substrate-specific system for a project.

standards.title: Glossary of paint and painting terms
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata records the 2002 edition as current and reconfirmed. It supplies paint and painting vocabulary rather than installation rules.
notes: The ontology retains coat, dry film, wet film, paint material and complete paint system as different concepts.

standards.title: Guide to the properties of paints for buildings, Part 0: General information on the specification, purchasing and testing of paints
standards.current_publication_note: The 2006 edition is current and was reconfirmed in 2016 according to public metadata. It is a general product-properties guide rather than a direct Housing Provisions reference.
notes: Colour, gloss, volume solids and performance evidence are attributes of selected coatings, not separate pieces of building geometry.

standards.title: Guide to long-life coatings for concrete and masonry, Part 4: Latex — Textured coatings — Aggregate-filled
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata lists the 1999 edition as current and reconfirmed in 2013. It supports aggregate-filled texture-coating identity on concrete and masonry.
notes: Texture and high build can mask minor visual irregularities but do not convert an unsound or leaking substrate into compliant construction.

standards.title: Guide to hazardous paint management, Part 2: Lead paint in residential, public and commercial buildings
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata lists the 2017 edition as current. It supports assessment and management routing for existing lead paint in non-industrial buildings.
notes: Lead content is hazardous-material evidence attached to an existing coating sample or field; it must not be inferred from colour, age alone or generic paint geometry.

standards.title: Steel for the reinforcement of concrete
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata identifies the 2019 edition as the current steel-reinforcement product standard. It supports bars, coils and welded mesh but does not replace AS 3600 detailing or project certification.
notes: Product designation, ductility, marking and traceability are evidence attributes; they cannot be inferred from a modelled cylinder or mesh texture.

standards.title: Specification and supply of concrete
standards.current_publication_note: The 2007 edition, incorporating Amendments 1 and 2 and reconfirmed in 2017, remains current in public metadata. It supports supplied-concrete identity and specification, not universal mix values.
notes: A delivery docket, slump result or strength result is evidence about concrete, not a separate physical member.

standards.title: Formwork for concrete, Part 1: Specifications
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata lists the 2018 specifications edition as current. It supports formwork documentation and formed-concrete surface identity, not unformed finishes or coatings.
notes: Off-form appearance is a concrete surface result and evidence state, not a coating layer automatically left by formwork.

standards.title: Formwork for concrete, Part 2: Design and construction
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public metadata lists this interim 2023 publication as current and covering design, erection and removal of formwork and supporting falsework.
notes: Temporary-work member sizes, loads, bracing, foundations, sequence and stripping state require design evidence and must not be generated from shape alone.

standards.title: Prefabricated concrete elements, Part 1: General requirements
standards.current_publication_note: The current second edition was published in 2024 and supersedes AS 3850.1:2015. It covers materials, components and equipment for manufacture, including cast-in lifting and brace inserts, but not in-service element design.
notes: A lifting insert can remain physically cast in while a lifting clutch is temporary equipment; neither is automatically a final structural connection.

standards.title: Prefabricated concrete elements, Part 2: Building construction
standards.current_publication_note: The current 2024 edition supersedes the 2015 edition and Amendment 1:2018. Its public scope includes planning, manufacture, design, casting, transport, erection and incorporation of prefabricated elements.
notes: The ontology records manufacture, transport, erection and final states separately because supports, actions and connections change between them.

standards.title: Piling — Design and installation
standards.current_publication_note: The 2009 edition incorporating Amendment 1:2010 is current in public metadata and referenced by NCC Volume Two H1D12. It is not a direct Housing Provisions Schedule 2 reference, so the locked direct count remains unchanged.
notes: Pile type, geotechnical resistance, installation method, verification and cut-off level remain project inputs rather than inferred geometry.

standards.title: Steel prestressing materials, Part 1: General requirements
standards.current_publication_note: Public standard catalogues list the 2007 edition as active/current for high-tensile steel tendons used to prestress concrete and similar structures.
notes: Prestressing force and losses are attributes or analysis results; strand, wire and bar are physical objects.

standards.title: Prestressing anchorages
standards.current_publication_note: The 2003 edition was reconfirmed in Australia in 2016 and remains current in public metadata. It supports anchorage and coupling product identity and prototype performance.
notes: The standard does not replace design of the surrounding concrete anchorage zone.

standards.title: Bar chairs in reinforced concrete — Product requirements and test methods
standards.current_publication_note: The 2015 edition is the current product and test-method reference used in current Australian reinforcement guidance for bar chairs.
notes: Chair material and strength grade are selected attributes; one generic cone cannot represent every chair type or exposure condition.

standards.title: General purpose and blended cements
standards.current_publication_note: Public metadata and current Australian industry guidance identify AS 3972:2010 as the current general-purpose and blended-cement standard.
notes: Cement is a binder constituent; it is not an accepted synonym for concrete, mortar or grout.

standards.title: Aggregates and rock for engineering purposes, Part 1: Concrete aggregates
standards.current_publication_note: Standards Australia public content history lists the 2014 concrete-aggregate edition as current.
notes: Particle grading and source are material attributes; the final concrete element normally models aggregate as part of the composite rather than thousands of individual stones.

standards.title: Chemical admixtures for concrete, mortar and grout, Part 1: Admixtures for concrete
standards.current_publication_note: Public catalogue metadata lists the 2000 edition, reconfirmed in 2018, as current for concrete chemical admixtures.
notes: An admixture is a controlled batch constituent and generally does not remain as a separately drawable layer after hardening.

standards.title: Plywood — Formwork
standards.current_publication_note: The 2016 edition is current and supersedes AS 6669:2007. It supports manufacture, grading, finishing and branding of plywood specifically used for concrete formwork.
notes: Formwork plywood is temporary unless explicitly documented as permanent formwork; its phenolic face is not an applied finish on the hardened member.

standards.title: Built-in components for masonry construction, Part 2: Connectors and accessories
standards.current_publication_note: The 2020 edition is current in public metadata. It covers built-in masonry connectors and accessories but excludes wall ties, lintels and shelf angles, damp-proof courses and flashings, termite protection and structural bed-joint reinforcement from its own product scope.
notes: It is relevant through broader masonry design paths, not a direct Housing Provisions Schedule 2 reference in this registry.

standards.title: Masonry units, pavers, flags and segmental retaining wall units, Part 1: Masonry units
standards.current_publication_note: The 2008 edition was reconfirmed in Australia in 2020 and is listed as current in public metadata for masonry units used with AS 3700.
notes: Unit material, geometry, exposure classification and product test evidence remain separate from the wall assembly that uses the unit.

standards.title: Masonry units, segmental pavers and flags — Methods of test
standards.current_publication_note: The multipart 2003 test-method series and its current amendments remain active in public catalogues. The registry groups the series for provenance rather than copying nineteen separate test procedures.
notes: Dimensions, strength, durability and other test results are evidence attributes, not additional physical building objects.

standards.title: Limes and limestones, Part 1: Limes for building
standards.current_publication_note: The 1997 edition was reconfirmed in Australia in 2016 and remains current in public metadata for quicklime and hydrated lime intended for building.
notes: Building lime is a constituent of selected mortar or render mixes; lime putty and a completed render coat remain different physical material states.

standards.title: Guide to plastering
standards.current_publication_note: Withdrawn on 29 November 2018. The current CPCCSP3001 training-unit description still names it, so it is retained for terminology history only and must not be presented as a current standard or compliance path.
notes: Current project requirements must come from adopted law, current standards, specifications and selected-system evidence.

standards.title: Security door and window screens, Part 1: Classification and performance
standards.current_publication_note: Published in 2023 and current with amendment 1:2024. It supersedes AS 5039:2008 and covers classification and performance for hinged, sliding, folding, removable and fixed security door and window screens.
notes: Security classification is evidence about the complete tested product and compatible installation, not a visual property of mesh or grille infill.

standards.title: Security door and window screens, Part 2: Installation
standards.current_publication_note: Published in 2024 as the current installation part of the restructured AS 5039 series, replacing the former AS 5040 pathway.
notes: Host substrate, clearances, anchors, frame and product installation must be retained together; generic fixing geometry cannot establish conformity.

standards.title: Security door and window screens, Part 3: Methods of test
standards.current_publication_note: Published in 2023 as the current test-method part of the AS 5039 series and superseding AS 5041:2003.
notes: Test results and classifications are evidence fields; test apparatus and procedures are not physical installed building objects.

standards.title: Household and similar electrical appliances — Safety, Part 2.95: Particular requirements for vertically moving garage doors for residential use
standards.current_publication_note: Published on 29 November 2024. It and the 2020 edition remain current during the stated three-year transition; the 2024 edition is scheduled to supersede 2020 on 29 November 2027, subject to regulator adoption.
notes: It supports the identity of the drive, controls and protective devices. Product electrical conformity and safe-force settings cannot be inferred from a SketchUp component.

standards.title: Waterproofing membranes for external above-ground use, Part 1: Materials
standards.current_publication_note: Published on 14 September 2012 and listed as current in public standards metadata. NCC 2022 Volume Two H2D8 calls it up for membrane materials in applicable external waterproofing systems; it is not counted as a direct reference from the separate ABCB Housing Provisions Schedule 2 column.
notes: Material conformity belongs to the identified membrane product or tested system. A generic liquid or sheet drawn in SketchUp is not evidence of AS 4654.1 conformity.

standards.title: Waterproofing membranes for external above-ground use, Part 2: Design and installation
standards.current_publication_note: Published on 14 September 2012 as the current second edition. NCC 2022 Volume Two H2D8 calls it up for design and installation of applicable external above-ground waterproofing; it is not counted as a direct reference from the separate ABCB Housing Provisions Schedule 2 column.
notes: It supports system anatomy including substrates, membranes, outlets, overflows, drainage cells, flashings, movement treatment, penetrations and terminations. Exact dimensions and details require the licensed standard, adopted NCC and project conditions.

standards.title: Timber — Natural durability ratings
standards.current_publication_note: Published on 23 December 2022 and current in public standards metadata. It provides natural-durability ratings for timber; those ratings concern untreated heartwood and are not preservative-treatment hazard classes.
notes: Do not infer natural durability from colour or a broad trade name, do not apply a heartwood rating to sapwood, and do not treat durability as proof of termite resistance.

standards.title: Preservative-treated wood-based products, Part 1: Products and treatment
standards.current_publication_note: Published on 16 April 2021 and current in public metadata. It consolidates product and treatment requirements for preservative-treated wood-based products and identifies treatment evidence separately from natural durability.
notes: Hazard class, preservative, penetration and retention are product-evidence fields. Green colour, species name or an unmarked model object is not sufficient evidence of treatment suitability.
